title: Algebraic transport of unit-normalized site composition and identity
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be small sites in a fixed larger sheaf universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $v:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ be functors whose precomposition functors preserve sheaves of sets. For $w=v,u,uv,\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$, let $L_w$ be the specified inverse image, left adjoint to $P_w(H)=H\circ w$, with unit $\eta^w$, constructed by the comma colimit and sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction]. Assume $L_v,L_u,L_{uv}$ preserve finite limits. Lift these functors to ring sheaves and module sheaves by applying them to operation maps through the canonical finite-product and terminal-object comparisons, with the underlying-sheaf identifications of [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. Module sheaves are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

There is a unique natural isomorphism $\gamma:L_{uv}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_uL_v$ satisfying
$$P_vP_u(\gamma_H)\circ\eta^{uv}_H=P_v(\eta^u_{L_vH})\circ\eta^v_H.$$
Equivalently, for every $W\in\mathcal C$ and $s\in H(W)$, it satisfies $\gamma_H((uv)^{-1}s)=u^{-1}(v^{-1}s)$ in $(L_uL_vH)(uv(W))$, where each inverse-image section is the corresponding unit image. This section equation alone determines the natural isomorphism.

For $i=0,1$ put $L_0=L_{uv}$, $L_1=L_uL_v$, and let $p^i_{A,B}:L_i(A\times B)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_iA\times L_iB$ and $p^i_*:L_i(*)\xrightarrow{\sim}*$ be the canonical comparisons. Then
$$p^1_{A,B}\gamma_{A\times B}=(\gamma_A\times\gamma_B)p^0_{A,B},\qquad p^1_*\gamma_*=p^0_*.$$
For every commutative ring sheaf $R$ on $\mathcal C$, $\gamma_R$ is a ring-sheaf isomorphism. For every $R$-module sheaf $M$, $\gamma_M$ is a natural additive isomorphism semilinear through $\gamma_R$: $\gamma_M(a m)=\gamma_R(a)\gamma_M(m)$ on all local sections. These maps respect zero, one, addition, multiplication and module scalar action.

The identity adjunction unit $\eta^{\mathrm{id}}_H:H\to L_{\mathrm{id}}H$ is an isomorphism for every set sheaf $H$ (identifying $P_{\mathrm{id}}$ with the identity). On commutative ring sheaves it is a ring isomorphism, and for every $R$-module $M$ its component is additive and semilinear through $\eta^{\mathrm{id}}_R$.
